item.title: 2 right-wing provocateurs facing election-related charges in Minnesota

item.title: Police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death
item.description: Police have closed the investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after a post-mortem found she died accidentally.

item.title: Canada and EU drop associate membership plan in bid to deepen ties
item.description: Canada and the European Union will pursue closer ties but have dropped a proposal for associate EU membership, according to a joint declaration ahead of Thursday’s summit in Montreal. Prime Minister Mark Carney is seeking to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US, despite warnings from Donald Trump.

item.title: Judge denies the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots
item.description: While the judge rejected the Department of Justice's unprecedented demand in California, the case isn't over yet and will likely be appealed.

item.title: Peltola campaign under fire after report it recruited 2nd Dan Sullivan in Senate race
item.description: Alaskans for Mary said it "has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."

item.title: Early vote one week out shows Democratic enthusiasm in Texas, Georgia: Analysis
item.description: With just one week out to the 2026 midterms, an ABC News analysis of the early vote in the key states of Texas and Georgia shows signs of enthusiasm for Democrats.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir remembers the life and legacy of Barbara Barrie
item.description: The Oscar, Emmy and Tony nominee appeared in numerous films and TV series, including her role as the supportive mother in “Breaking Away.” David Muir remembers her legacy.

item.title: 10-year-old girl reported abducted from Oregon apartment found safe: Police
item.description: Officers responded to an apartment complex in Canby at 1:47 a.m. Wednesday for the reported kidnapping, the Canby Police Department said.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, civil rights icon, dies at 96
item.description: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers, has died at 96, her family said.

item.title: Some wellness peptides will become widely available, HHS says
item.description: "The policy does not ... establish clinical safety and effectiveness," HHS said.

item.title: Spain rail crash came after train ordered to go in error: minister
item.description: A rail collision in Spain that claimed at least 68 lives on Wednesday came after a train was ordered to go in "error" despite a technical failure that halted all services, the transport minister said. The first findings about the accident in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha are likely to revive questions about rail safety in Spain after another high-speed collision in January killed 46 people. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.

item.title: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
item.description: The Department of Health and Human Services will let small compounding pharmacies make six peptides that haven't been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. It may not be enough to meet demand.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil's true leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro's defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Fabio de Sa e Silva, Associate Professor of International Studies at the University of Oklahoma. He says that an attempt by Bolsonaro to turn a domestic dispute into a wider international issue "will not be successful", explaining that he is likely going to be "losing the grip of the opposition, there is a vacuum now that others will seek to occupy" and that it's unlikely that the United States will "get involved into questioning the results of the Brazilian election".

item.title: Rail safety questioned after Spain suffers second fatal high-speed train crash in a year
item.description: Questions are being raised about Spain's rail safety as authorities launch an official investigation into the cause of Wednesday's high-speed train collision, which killed at least 68 people and wounded around 100 more, in the country's second fatal rail crash this year.

item.title: EU natural gas prices top €100 for first time since 2022
item.description: As winter approaches, the price of European natural gas topped €100 / megawatt hour, its highest level since 2022. The EU says it's not worried about supplies, although its storage facilities are only 72% full, but warns households of a 'difficult' season to come. Also in the show - the UK government tries to cushion the impact of high energy bills, and 200 passengers are stranded in Cambodia after their multi-year cruise was cancelled because of high fuel costs.

item.title: WATCH: How Trump’s economic policies could shape the midterms
item.description: ABC News’ Alex Presha examines voters’ economic concerns, while KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk discusses interest rates, consumer confidence and financial uncertainty.

item.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
item.description: In tonight's edition, a summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opens in Moscow with the Kremlin describing their countries as natural allies against the West. Also, Nigerian investigators say that dozens of detained miners who died in a crowded jail cell screamed for help as jailors ignored their suffering. And ahead of the Youth Olympics in Senegal, Kenya's ramping up support of its women's sportspeople.

item.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
item.description: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.

item.title: Historic gains for Arab-majority parties in Israeli election
item.description: Two Arab-majority parties are set to win a historic 19 seats in total, amid a record turnout at the polls in Israel on Tuesday. Voters from the community, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation and who make up around 20 percent of the population, have been enraged by the Netanyahu government's ultra-nationalist Jewish vision for the country and the Palestinian territories. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Top US federal judge who handled 9/11, Trump, Maduro cases dies aged 92
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, a top US judge who was handling the trial against deposed Venezuelan leader Nicholas Maduro and previously oversaw lawsuits stemming from the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Centre and multiple cases involving President Donald Trump, died on Wednesday aged 92.

item.title: Bolsonaro's escape to the US: How it happened
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida by private plane Wednesday after fleeing his country in defiance of a court order to surrender his passport. Bolsonaro, who lost a runoff election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday, is under investigation in Brazil for alleged corruption and money laundering and, with his defeat, is set to lose parliamentary immunity. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Amid uncertainty over EU aid, Vitalii Kim insists Ukraine has no choice but to fight for motherland
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Vitalii Kim, Minister for Veterans Affairs of Ukraine. “If Europe will not support us, we also will fight because it's our motherland,” says Kim, insisting that Ukraine's determination to resist Russian aggression will endure regardless of the outcome of negotiations over European financial assistance. Yet behind this assertion of national resolve lies a more complex reality: a country confronting not only the immediate pressures of war, but also its mounting psychological, social and institutional consequences.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro insists he is 'leader of Brazil' despite losing election run-off
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro has called himself the "leader of Brazil" - despite losing the presidential election.

item.title: Bolsonaro flees Brazil for US after election defeat
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro's clandestine escape to the United States bewildered Brazil and triggered a frantic search for his whereabouts. The Supreme Court had ordered the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro to forfeit his passports after his electoral loss on Sunday, amid fears he would leave the country due to ongoing investigations against him. But the defeated right-wing presidential candidate failed to hand them in, choosing instead to flee to the US via Argentina and Ecuador. FRANCE 24's Tim Vickery reports from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Which way will Israel break? Netanyahu still in it after election night surprises
item.description: In Israel, the surprises only start with election night: they're still counting ballots in a vote that featured the highest turnout in decades, historic inroads by Arab parties, Benjamin Netanyahu’s worst result since 1999 and yet Israel’s longest-serving prime minister still has a path to staying in power. As we await the definitive makeup of the next parliament, our panel breaks out the calculators and pie charts: in what scenario does Netanyahu survive? Is the issue with the right-wing Likud leader or his policies?

item.title: Spain high-speed train crash kills 68, injures over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said, in one of Europe's deadliest such disasters this century. The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country's rail safety, with the transport minister speaking of an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the collision. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Urda, south of Madrid.

item.title: 'Israeli electorate has moved rightward: Many underestimated extent of fracture in Israeli society'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Dr. Shira Efron, RAND's Distinguished Israel Policy Chair. “Many of us, myself included, underestimated the extent of the fracture in Israeli society.” It reflects a political system in which ideological polarisation, the rightward shift of the Jewish electorate and the contested legitimacy of Arab political participation have sharply narrowed the possibilities for coalition-building. Dr. Efron illustrates a political landscape in which Netanyahu’s governing bloc has lost ground, yet still has “more cards, or better cards, to play,” she argues, whether through another election, a national unity government or attempts to draw opposition partners into his orbit.

item.title: Putin woos African leaders as Moscow seeks to expand footprint in Africa
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sought to woo African leaders and government delegates on Wednesday as they gathered in Moscow for the third Russia-Africa Summit to discuss trade, security, arms deals and grain supplies as part of the Kremlin's strategic efforts to expand its footprint in Africa.

item.title: New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway
item.description: Jordan Neely was frightening fellow passengers. A former Marine named Daniel Penny put Neely into a chokehold, killing him. Journalist Anand Giridharadas investigates the incident in Man in the Mirror.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
item.description: The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.

item.title: Man who stabbed 10 on train asked passenger 'do you want to die?', court hears
item.description: A man who stabbed 10 people on a train heading to London asked one passenger "do you want to die?", a court has heard.

item.title: 'Si, se puede': US civil rights icon Dolores Huerta dies at 96
item.description: Influential US labour union co-founder, feminist, and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday in Bakersfield, California, her family said. Credited with coining the enduring "Si, se puede!" rallying cry later adapted by former US president Barack Obama, Huerta continued her activism on race, poverty, LGBTQ and women's rights issues until the last months of her life.

item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: US grants visa to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his immediate family landed in Miami, Florida on Wednesday after he refused to surrender his passports as ordered by his country's Supreme Court in connection with a money-laundering probe. The US State Department on Tuesday announced it had granted entry visas to the senator and his family. France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Israel election: What impact on Iran as the war in the Middle East continues?
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to face greater constraints as Israel’s caretaker prime minister following Tuesday’s election. However, experts say his government could retain significant powers, including the authority to wage war against Iran. So what impact will the election have on Israel’s approach to Iran? France 24’s International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley shares further insights.

item.title: France: Racist attack in Trappes deeply scars local community
item.description: It has been five days since a gunman opened fire in the Paris suburb of Trappes in a racist attack that left one person dead and five others injured. Over the weekend, hundreds of people marched through the town to pay tribute to the 26-year-old victim, Bossio Wangi, and show solidarity with his family. The attack has left a deep mark on the local community, and mediators have been mobilised to provide support. Eliza Herbert reports.

item.title: Defeated presidential candidate Bolsonaro lands in Miami after fleeing Brazil
item.description: Brazilian Senator ​Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday, where the United States government granted them ​entry visas after he refused to comply with a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. Bolsonaro lost Sunday's presidential election to leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

item.title: Ethiopia clashes push 50,000 to flee to Kenya
item.description: The outbreak of fighting between rival forces in southern Ethiopia last week has led some 50,000 people to seek refuge in neighbouring Kenya, the United Nations said Wednesday, citing local authorities.

item.title: Spain: PM Sanchez gives speech on train collision
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez addressed the nation from the site of the train collision in Toledo province, expressing his full solidarity with the victims, their families and all those injured in the tragedy. Earlier, Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer malfunction had disrupted the railway’s safety system. He said the RENFE train had been instructed to resume its journey despite an active stop signal, before crashing into the stationary IRYO train. The collision on Wednesday killed at least 64 people and injured 58 others. Rescue teams continue to search the wreckage for survivors and bodies. It is Spain’s second deadly high-speed rail collision this year, following a January crash that killed 46 people.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
item.description: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry.
